## Natural history notes

A medium-sized assassin bug characterized by an orange to reddish body, long dark legs banded with pale rings, narrow head, and a curved piercing beak tucked beneath the body. In Florida, the Ringed Assassin Bug is found in gardens, fields, forest edges, hammocks, pine flatwoods, parks, and shrubby vegetation where insect prey is common. It is a predatory true bug that stalks and ambushes caterpillars, flies, beetles, and other small arthropods, piercing prey with its beak and injecting digestive saliva; like other assassin bugs, it should be observed without handling because it can deliver a painful defensive bite.
